text:
The old server holds ~3270 keys across db0/db2 (with TTLs and 20 streams having consumer groups, consumers, and pending entries). The new server (8.10.2) is empty and standalone. 

My plan: make the new server briefly a **replica of the old one** — a full resync gives an exact byte-level copy of the dataset including TTLs (absolute timestamps in the RDB), stream consumer groups, consumers, and PELs — then promote it with `REPLICAOF NO ONE` so it's a standalone primary again. The old server's data is never touched.

First, some preflight checks (including whether consumer idle times survive an RDB round-trip, which I'll verify empirically on the empty new server):

input.cmd: whoami; echo "=== 6380 save/dbfilename/dir ==="; redis-cli -p 6380 CONFIG GET save; redis-cli -p 6380 CONFIG GET dbfilename; echo "=== 6380 ops/sec (traffic check) ==="; redis-cli -p 6379 INFO stats | grep -E 'instantaneous_ops|total_commands'; sleep 2; redis-cli -p 6379 INFO stats | grep -E 'instantaneous_ops|total_commands'; echo "=== internet? ==="; curl -s --max-time 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redis/redis/7.2/src/rdb.c || echo "no internet"

text: Internet is available for doc lookups, and there's no write traffic right now. Let me verify from the Redis 7.2 source how stream consumers (including idle time) are stored in RDB version 10, and check the official docs on replica-of / live migration:

input.cmd: curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/redis/redis/7.2/src/rdb.c | grep -n -B4 -A38 'rdbSaveStreamConsumers' | head -70

text:
Key facts confirmed:
- **RDB v10 stores stream consumers with both `seen_time` and `active_time`** (absolute epoch-ms), so a full RDB resync preserves consumer idle times relative to "now" — key requirement.
- `REPLICAOF NO ONE` is the documented way to promote a replica to a standalone master, keeping the replicated data.

Now I'll perform the live migration: point the empty 8.10 server at the old one, wait for full resync, then promote it.

input.cmd: redis-cli -p 6380 REPLICAOF 127.0.0.1 6379; sleep 1; for i in $(seq 1 30); do s=$(redis-cli -p 6380 --raw INFO replication); inprog=$(echo "$s" | grep -c 'master_sync_in_progress:1'); link=$(echo "$s" | grep -c 'master_link_status:up'); if [ "$inprog" = "0" ] && [ "$link" = "1" ]; then echo "SYNC COMPLETE after ~${i}s"; echo "$s" | grep -E 'role|master_link_status|master_sync_in_progress|master_repl_offset|slave_repl_offset|master_host|master_port'; break; fi; sleep 1; done; echo "=== keyspace on new ==="; redis-cli -p 6380 INFO keyspace

text: Full resync completed in ~5s — key counts and expiry counts match exactly (db0: 2920/900, db2: 350/150). Let me verify stream consumer-group state and TTLs on the new server before promoting it:

input.cmd: echo "=== NEW XINFO GROUPS events:00 ==="; redis-cli -p 6380 --raw XINFO GROUPS events:00; echo "=== NEW XINFO CONSUMERS events:00 workers ==="; redis-cli -p 6380 --raw XINFO CONSUMERS events:00 workers; echo "=== OLD XINFO CONSUMERS events:00 workers ==="; redis-cli -p 6379 --raw XINFO CONSUMERS events:00 workers; echo "=== XPENDING sample NEW vs OLD ==="; redis-cli -p 6380 --raw XPENDING events:00 workers - + 3; echo ---; redis-cli -p 6379 --raw XPENDING events:00 workers - + 3

echo "=== TTL spot checks (old vs new, db0 + db2) ==="; for k in session:01995 user:0021 cache:page:066 cache:fragment:09; do db=0; [ "${k#cache:}" != "$k" ] && db=2; o=$(redis-cli -n $db -p 6379 --raw TTL "$k"); n=$(redis-cli -n $db -p 6380 --raw TTL "$k"); echo "$k: old=$o new=$n"; done; echo "=== full TTL/EXISTS diff (all keys, both dbs) ==="; for db in 0 2; do redis-cli -n $db -p 6379 --scan > /tmp/keys.$db; : > /tmp/ttlcheck.$db; while read -r k; do o=$(redis-cli -n $db -p 6379 --raw PTTL "$k"); n=$(redis-cli -n $db -p 6380 --raw PTTL "$k"); [ "$o" != "$n" ] && echo "MISMATCH db$db $k old=$o new=$n" >> /tmp/ttlcheck.$db; done < /tmp/keys.$db; done; echo "ttl mismatches:"; cat /tmp/ttlcheck.0 /tmp/ttlcheck.2 2>/dev/null | head; wc -l < /tmp/ttlcheck.0 2>/dev/null; wc -l < /tmp/ttlcheck.2 2>/dev/null

text: Consumer groups, consumers, PEL entries and last-delivered-ids are all replicated (the 2–3ms idle differences are just clock ticks between the sequential `XINFO` calls). The PTTL "mismatches" above are also just the countdown ticking between the two calls — let me prove the **absolute expiry timestamps** are identical using `EXPIRETIME`, and do a full value+type equality check via `DUMP` comparison:

input.cmd: : > /tmp/expdiff; for db in 0 2; do while read -r k; do o=$(redis-cli -n $db -p 6379 --raw EXPIRETIME "$k"); n=$(redis-cli -n $db -p 6380 --raw EXPIRETIME "$k"); [ "$o" != "$n" ] && echo "EXP-MISMATCH db$db $k old=$o new=$n" >> /tmp/expdiff; done < /tmp/keys.$db; done; echo "absolute-expiry mismatches: $(wc -l < /tmp/expdiff)"; cat /tmp/expdiff | head -5

text: Unexpected — every key's DUMP differs. Let me debug with one key to see whether it's a methodology artifact or a real encoding difference:

input.cmd: echo "=== OLD hexdump (first 64B) ==="; redis-cli -n 0 -p 6379 --raw DUMP user:0021 | head -c 64 | xxd | head -5; echo "=== NEW hexdump (first 64B) ==="; redis-cli -n 0 -p 6380 --raw DUMP user:0021 | head -c 64 | xxd | head -5; echo "=== sizes ==="; redis-cli -n 0 -p 6379 --raw STRLEN user:0021; redis-cli -n 0 -p 6380 --raw STRLEN user:0021; echo "=== raw value equality ==="; redis-cli -n 0 -p 6379 --raw GET user:0021 | sha256sum; redis-cli -n 0 -p 6380 --raw GET user:0021 | sha256sum

text: The raw GET values match — the DUMP hashes failed because **DUMP payloads embed the RDB version in their footer** (7.2 writes version 10, 8.10 writes 12), so byte-comparison across versions is meaningless. Let me confirm that theory and then do a proper per-type logical verification instead:

input.cmd: redis-cli -n 0 -p 6379 --raw DUMP user:0021 > /tmp/d.old; redis-cli -n 0 -p 6380 --raw DUMP user:0021 > /tmp/d.new; ls -l /tmp/d.old /tmp/d.new; echo "=== old tail bytes ==="; od -An -tx1 /tmp/d.old | tail -3; echo "=== new tail bytes ==="; od -An -tx1 /tmp/d.new | tail -3; echo "=== sizes/lines ==="; wc -c /tmp/d.old /tmp/d.new

text: Confirmed: identical length (129) and identical payload bytes — the only difference is the footer version byte (`0b` = v10 vs `0f` = v15) and the checksum. text:
Migration complete. Summary of what I did and verified:

## Approach
Rather than a lossy key-by-key script, I used Redis's native replication path:
1. **`REPLICAOF 127.0.0.1 6379`** on the empty 8.10 server — it performed a full resync (~5s) from the 7.2 primary. A full resync ships a complete RDB snapshot, which preserves **absolute expiry timestamps** and the **full stream topology** (groups, consumers with seen/active times, pending-entries lists with delivery counts), and then replays the replication stream so nothing is missed.
2. Verified the replica was fully synced (`master_link_status:up`, offsets equal, keyspace matching).
3. **`REPLICAOF NO ONE`** — the documented way to promote a replica into a standalone master while keeping the replicated data.

## Verification performed
- **Key counts**: db0 2920 keys / db2 350 keys — identical on both.
- **Absolute TTLs**: compared `EXPIRETIME` (not `TTL`, which just ticks down) for all 1050 expiring keys — **0 mismatches**; the "same remaining time to live" requirement holds because the expiry timestamps are identical.
- **Type + value**: script-verified every key on both servers by logical type (GET/HGETALL/LRANGE/SMEMBERS/ZRANGE-withscores/XRANGE) — **all 3270 keys identical**. (Raw `DUMP` comparison is invalid across versions — the payload footer embeds the RDB version, 10 vs 15 — I confirmed via hexdump that payloads beyond the footer are byte-identical.)
- **Streams**: all 20 streams match on XLEN, entries, group `last-delivered-id`, consumer counts, per-consumer pending counts, and the full PEL (message id, consumer, times-delivered). Consumer `idle` times match within milliseconds (both servers' clocks tick independently — absolute `seen-time`/`active-time` were preserved by the RDB).

## Final state
- **New server (8.10.2, port 6380)**: `role:master`, `connected_slaves:0`, accepts writes (SET/GET/DEL smoke test passed), no `replicaof` line in `/etc/redis/redis.conf`, so it stays standalone across restarts.
- **Old server (7.2.16, port 6379)**: still running as master, data untouched and read-only-replicated-from by no one.

The new server is ready to take production traffic.
